title: Immunomodulation, monolayer repair and extracellular matrix remodelling of primary human AT-II cells during cyclic sinusoidal stretch
summary:
The lungs are exposed to unphysiological stress during mechanical ventilation. This can lead to the development or worsening of lung damage. Involved processes are tissue disruption, inflammatory processes and tissue remodelling. A prospective option to improve respiratory efficiency while reducing lung injury is to exploit the potential of the temporal characteristic (time course) of the ventilation profile. In order to gain a better understanding of how the mechanism of lung response and mechanical strain are related, cell culture experiments are a useful tool. Therefore, we need primary lung epithelial cells (AT-2), which will be obtained from otherwise discarded tissue (from lung transplants or partial resections). The use of human cells increases the relevance and transferability of the results. Freshly harvested cells reflect the characteristic functions of the original tissue, leading to representative results.

In a first step, the effects of different strain profiles on the inflammatory response of AT-2 cells will be investigated. The focus will be on intensity and mediation of inflammation. In a second step, the effects of different strain profiles on the processes involved in tissue repair (cell migration, cell adhesion, cell spreading, cell division and cell death) will be investigated. In a third step, the effects of the different strain profiles on the release of matrix and matrix remodelling molecules (serving tissue regeneration) as well as the release of surfactant proteins will be the focus of the investigations.

interventions.name: Extraction of cells from Lung tissue remains

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Consent to participate in the study
- Planned (partial) lung resection due to central lung tumour or tumour in the upper lobe; transplantation or pneumothorax
Exclusion criteria:
- No consent to participate in the study or unable to give consent
- Pneumonia
